identity.title: Ring structure in the MWC 480 disk revealed by ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: we present high angular resolution ALMA images of 1.3 mm continuum emission from the protoplanetary disk around MWC 480 (also frequently called HD 31648), and subsequently model the disk with hydrodynamic simulations

evidence.quote: MWC 480 is a Herbig Ae star located at a Gaia DR2 distance[^1] of $161.8_{-2}^{+2}\,\rm{pc}$
MWC 480 is a Herbig Ae star located at a Gaia DR2 distance[^1] of $161.8_{-2}^{+2}\,\rm{pc}$

question.value: What is the dust ring/gap structure of the MWC 480 disk at 1.3 mm, and can a planet–disk interaction explain it (planet mass)?

evidence.quote: subsequently model the disk with hydrodynamic simulations to infer the mass of a possible planet within the disk.
as part of the Cycle 4 program (ID: 2016.1.01164.S; PI: G. Herczeg) on August 27, 2017
We observed MWC 480 with ALMA in Band 6 (230 GHz)
The observation was conducted using 47 12 m antennas with baselines ranging from 21 to 3638 m.
The resulting beam size is $0.17^{\prime\prime}\times0.11^{\prime\prime}$, corresponding to a physical scale of $27.5 \times 17.8$ au
The rms noise level of the image is ${\sim}\,0.07\,\rm{mJy/beam}$.
The on-source time was 4 minutes and the precipitable water vapor (PWV) was 0.5 mm during the integration.
